title: The Salvation of the Soul and the Unity of the Church
english: The shadow is pre-ordained to distinguish itself from the truth; it means this: in this life, finding myself in the shadow of the wings, I hope to come upon those very wings, being carried on wings by virtue and spiritual intellect. But the wings of God are His sheltering powers, or the lofty thoughts about Him.

The passing away of lawlessness shows that it is temporary (Ps 56:2). And Paul indeed writes in Hebrews that the enjoyment of sin is temporary (Heb 13:5). It is not as if lawlessness were passing away having begun from a certain time; for he says something about it: it shall be neither from the beginning nor unto the age (Ps 56:3).

But the Most High is not in vain (Ps 56:3). For since lawlessness is clinging and low-lying, the one being delivered from it cries out toward the Most High, so that by lifting himself up with the cry, he might become far from the harmful beast.

The Lord, sent from heaven to save, says: 'I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will' (John 6:38). For God sent this word of His and healed those wounded by their corruptions, as David himself says elsewhere. If anyone seeks to ask whether the one sent from heaven signifies a local emission from the physical heaven, it would seem absurd to attribute a local descent to God. For does the voice of heaven not signify the incorporeal and intellectual essence, according to 'Store up in the heavens' (Matt 6:20) and 'God is in the heaven above' (Ps 115:4)? Therefore, the one being in the form of God and being healed as God, having taken the form of a servant, [came] to men (Phil 2:6-7). And this is the sending from heaven, so that the Word of God might become flesh and, having appeared upon the earth, might walk among men (John 1:14). Peter also writes, initiating mysteries concerning the Holy Spirit: 'Now it has been announced to you through those who preached to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven' (1 Pet 1:2); for having been sent from the intellect...

That the Spirit may find essence in men, it was granted to those who preached to you (Ps 56:4b). Before this, saying, 'Those who before this, by despising, trampling me into reproach, were given, God having sent from heaven how I might be saved' (Ps 56:4c). For having seen the Son of God caring for my salvation, those acting shamefully and reproaching me, even though they trampled, God saved (Ps 56:4c.5a).

In the preceding verse, having said, 'He sent from heaven' (Ps 56:5a), not having said what was sent from heaven, he now interprets what mercy is and truth, the one rescuing his soul having become among enemies of those who trampled; for these are wild and wrathful dogs. Mercy is not otherwise according to the essence of truth; for both are the Savior (Ps 56:5b).

Sleep often signifies rest, as in, 'In peace I will lie down and sleep.' He does not wish to say this, that is, even if I was troubled being trampled by enemies and terrified by the dogs having taken me in the midst, but the trouble did not remain. For I slept having been troubled, not remaining awake being troubled, but I slept having cast away the trouble (Ps 56:5b).

This is a symbol of the woman continually weakened by the spirit, collapsing and not able to rise up completely, whom Jesus released from the snares of Satan, the daughter of Abraham (Ps 56:7b). Perhaps also everyone who thinks of the things below has a soul having become fallen, not able to contemplate the things above, is such a thing.

And you will perceive the people and those from circumcision, but the mortals from the idols having repented, as to become one church (Ps 56:10). Those having loved the Lord in incorruption, having come to the end of not being corrupted, the pillars through whom they work well, they raise up. For just as those doing the opposite do evil things, they make a forbidden pillar...
